| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=chrome.exe) by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search parent_process_name!=chrome.exe AND parent_process!="*\\Google\\Chrome\\*" AND parent_process_name!="MsMpEng.exe" AND parent_process_name!="taskmgr.exe" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=chrome.exe) by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search parent_process_name!=chrome.exe AND parent_process!="*\\Google\\Chrome\\*" AND parent_process_name!="MsMpEng.exe" AND parent_process_name!="taskmgr.exe" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Non-Chrome process tampering with Chrome passkey_enclave_state or Sync Data LevelDB AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts a non-Chrome process writing, copying, renaming, or deleting Chrome's passkey device-key store (passkey_enclave_state) or the synced-credential LevelDB. Copy-out feeds offline SDS/passkey recovery; deletion forces the device re-enrollment window that Silver/Golden Pass-ta-key abuse to register an attacker UV key. Rationale: Anchored on the exact artifacts named in the Unit 42 report — passkey_enclave_state (wrapped device key + SDS + PIN) and the Sync Data\LevelDB WebauthnCredentialSpecifics store — with any non-Chrome, non-Google-signed writer/deleter surfaced. Deletion maps to the forced re-enrollment window abused by Silver/Golden; copy-out maps to offline recovery. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1556
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OneDrive / enterprise backup agents syncing the Chrome profile folder
  • Chrome profile migration or roaming-profile tooling
  • Antivirus quarantine touching files under User Data
  • Admin manually deleting a corrupt Chrome profile to fix sync
  • Endpoint management agents wiping browser data on offboarding
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("OneDrive.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe","backup.exe","cbsystray.exe") and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName != "Google LLC"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is not Google-signed, OneDrive, or backup software; note ActionType (Delete vs Create/Modify) and whether a copy of passkey_enclave_state / LevelDB landed outside the profile. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill/quarantine the process, and treat the user's synced passkeys as compromised — trigger passkey re-enrollment and PIN rotation on the Google account. 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 (chrome.exe memory reads) on the same host, search for exfil of the copied store over the network, and review the Google account for new device enrollments or attacker-registered UV keys.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "passkey_enclave_state"
      or (FolderPath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\" and FolderPath has @"\Sync Data\LevelDB")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !~ "chrome.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName != "Google LLC"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Google\Chrome\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("OneDrive.exe","backup.exe","MsMpEng.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "passkey_enclave_state"
      or (TargetFilePath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\" and TargetFilePath has @"\Sync Data\LevelDB")
| where ActingProcessName !has @"\chrome.exe"
| where ActingProcessName !has @"\Google\Chrome\"
| where ActingProcessName !has @"\OneDrive.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, DvcAction, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Chrome Access to Chrome Passkey Enclave State / Sync LevelDB
id: b21c7e4f-9a08-4d13-8b6e-2f7c1a9d5e30
description: Detects non-Chrome processes writing, renaming or deleting Chrome's passkey_enclave_state device-key store or the Sync Data LevelDB (Unit 42 Pass-ta-key family)
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/03
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1556
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\passkey_enclave_state'
  selection_leveldb:
    TargetFilename|contains|all:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
      - '\Sync Data\LevelDB\'
  filter_chrome:
    Image|contains: '\Google\Chrome\'
  condition: (selection_name or selection_leveldb) and not filter_chrome
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\passkey_enclave_state OR *\\PASSKEY_ENCLAVE_STATE) OR (@TargetFilename:*\\User?Data\\* AND @TargetFilename:*\\LevelDB\\*)) NOT @Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE) NOT @Image:*\\Google\\Chrome\\*
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (TargetFileName=/\\passkey_enclave_state$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\.*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\/i)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\chrome\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\Google\\Chrome\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name=passkey_enclave_state OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search process_name!=chrome.exe AND process_name!="*\\Google\\Chrome\\*" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name=passkey_enclave_state OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search process_name!=chrome.exe AND process_name!="*\\Google\\Chrome\\*" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Command line referencing Chrome passkey_enclave_state or Sync Data LevelDB path AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts LOLBins/scripts (cmd, powershell, esentutl, robocopy, xcopy) invoked with Chrome's passkey store path on the command line — the tooling-based variant of Pass-ta-key local reconnaissance that enumerates relying parties, usernames and encrypted passkey material. Rationale: Targets the article's stated local-recon step (reading credential IDs, relying parties and usernames from Sync Data\LevelDB) plus the passkey_enclave_state path from the Unit 42 report, catching the copy/enumeration variant that uses native tooling rather than in-process API reads. Lower confidence/hunting tier because sophisticated malware reads via API and leaves nothing on the command line. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
ATT&CKT1217 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Support/IT scripts backing up or clearing a Chrome profile
  • Forensic/DFIR triage collection referencing the LevelDB path
  • Browser-data migration utilities
  • Developer debugging Chrome sync with the path in a script
  • Security tooling that inventories browser credential stores
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","MsSense.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and not (AccountName has_any ("svc-dfir","admin-backup"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the full command line and parent process — is this an admin/DFIR script, a migration tool, or an unexpected LOLBin (esentutl/robocopy/powershell) run by a standard user? Check the executing account and host role. 2) Contain: if unauthorized, isolate the host and kill the process; preserve any output/copy of the passkey store for IR and rotate the affected Google account passkeys. 3) Hunt: pivot on the parent process and user to UC1/UC2 (chrome memory reads and file tamper), check for archive/exfil of the collected data, and sweep the fleet for the same command-line pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("passkey_enclave_state", @"Sync Data\LevelDB")
| where ProcessCommandLine has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data" or ProcessCommandLine has "passkey_enclave_state"
| where FileName !~ "chrome.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName !~ "chrome.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("passkey_enclave_state", @"Sync Data\LevelDB")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "passkey_enclave_state"
| where TargetProcessName !has @"\chrome.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Command Line Referencing Chrome Passkey Store Path
id: c9d4f2a7-1e63-4b58-a0c2-7d9e5f81b3a6
description: Detects processes invoked with Chrome's passkey_enclave_state or Sync Data LevelDB path on the command line (Unit 42 Pass-ta-key local recon / copy-out)
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/03
tags:
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1217
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1555.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'passkey_enclave_state'
      - '\Sync Data\LevelDB'
  filter:
    Image|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @CommandLine:(*passkey_enclave_state* OR *PASSKEY_ENCLAVE_STATE* OR *Sync?Data\\LevelDB*) NOT @Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/passkey_enclave_state|Sync Data\\LevelDB/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\chrome\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*passkey_enclave_state*" OR Processes.process="*Sync Data\\LevelDB*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process_name!=chrome.exe | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*passkey_enclave_state*" OR Processes.process="*Sync Data\\LevelDB*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process_name!=chrome.exe | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] AnyDesk silent/unattended install used for DragonForce access · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] LockBit payload execution via PsExec service (PsExecSvc.exe → 1.exe/LBB.exe) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
RDP re-enable + EDR/Defender disable batch script (LockBit intrusion) AIInstallation High
Hunts the post-access batch script observed in the leaked-LockBit-builder case that enabled RDP by setting fDenyTSConnections to 0 and disabled endpoint defenses before ransomware deployment. Anchors on the exact registry value/data pair the article's script wrote. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim registry write from the article's disable-defenses batch script (HKLM\...\Control\Terminal Server \ fDenyTSConnections = 0) which turns RDP on; pairs it with reg.exe execution to keep fidelity high. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/lockbit-3-0-based-custom-targeted-ransomware/112375/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/lockbit-ransomware-builder-leaked-online-by-angry-developer/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112 T1021.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT admin legitimately enabling RDP on a new server build via a provisioning script
  • GPO/DSC/Intune configuration baseline that manages fDenyTSConnections
  • MSP onboarding automation that turns on RDP for remote management
  • Server 2016 role-setup wizards that toggle Remote Desktop
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","omadmclient.exe","gpscript.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating account and parent process of the reg.exe/registry write; confirm whether the same host also saw EDR/Defender service stops in the surrounding minutes. 2) Contain: isolate the host, disable the account used to write the value, and re-set fDenyTSConnections to 1 if the change was unauthorized. 3) Hunt: pivot on the account across DeviceLogonEvents for RDP (LogonType 10) and search for PsExecSvc.exe/named ransomware payloads (1.exe, LBB.exe) and Defender-tamper events fleet-wide.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Control\Terminal Server"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "fDenyTSConnections"
| where RegistryValueData == "0"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("SystemSettings.exe","ServerManager.exe","mmc.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\reg.exe"
| where CommandLine has "fDenyTSConnections" and CommandLine has_any ("/d 0","/d 0x0")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: RDP Enabled via fDenyTSConnections Registry Modification
id: 8f2b1c40-6d3a-4d1e-9a7b-2f0c9e441a11
description: Detects setting fDenyTSConnections to 0 under the Terminal Server control key, matching the RDP-enable step of the leaked-LockBit-builder intrusion at Brazilian educational institutions.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/incidents-at-brazilian-educational-institutions/120803/
author: SOC Detection Engineering

  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: '\Control\Terminal Server'
    Details: 'DWORD (0x00000000)'
  selection_value:
    TargetObject|endswith: '\fDenyTSConnections'
  condition: selection and selection_value
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 (@Image:(*\\reg.exe OR *\\REG.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*fDenyTSConnections* OR *FDENYTSCONNECTIONS*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/reg\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/fDenyTSConnections/i
| CommandLine=/\/d\s+0(x0)?/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Control\\Terminal Server*" Registry.registry_value_name="fDenyTSConnections" Registry.registry_value_data="0" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
LockBit payload execution via PsExec service (PsExecSvc.exe → 1.exe/LBB.exe) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the manual lateral deployment of the custom LockBit build from the leaked builder: the sample was configured without psexec_netspread, so operators used PsExec (PsExecSvc.exe) to remotely launch ransomware binaries named 1.EXE and LBB.exe. Targets the impact/deployment step, not generic PsExec admin use. Rationale: Uses the article's verbatim payload names (1.EXE, LBB.exe) and the PsExecSvc.exe service the operators relied on for manual spread after building a variant without psexec_netspread; combining parent + payload names keeps the otherwise-generic 1.exe fidelity acceptable. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/lockbit-3-0-based-custom-targeted-ransomware/112375/ • https://www.intel471.com/blog/dragonforce-ransomware
ATT&CKT1486 T1569.002 T1570
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate sysadmin using Sysinternals PsExec for remote software rollout (PsExecSvc.exe as parent)
  • Automation/RMM that names a tool 1.exe in a temp build path
  • Software packaging test binaries transiently named 1.exe
  • Remote patch scripts pushed via PsExec across a fleet
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\SCCM\\","\\ccmcache\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the SHA256 and full path of the spawned binary and the source host driving PsExecSvc.exe; check for mass DeviceFileEvents FileRenamed/FileModified bursts on the same device. 2) Contain: network-isolate affected hosts, block the payload hash, and disable the deploying account. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host where PsExecSvc.exe appeared (USN Journal .KEY artifacts corroborate historic spread), look for kill_defender/Defender-uninstall events and wallpaper/registry changes indicative of LockBit encryption.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "PsExecSvc.exe"
    or FileName in~ ("1.exe","LBB.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (ParentProcessName endswith "\\PsExecSvc.exe")
    or (NewProcessName endswith "\\1.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\LBB.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Potato privilege-escalation tooling (GodPotato / SweetPotato / BadPotato) AIExploitation High
Hunts the SeImpersonate token-abuse tools the article attributes to the observed privilege-escalation activity in these intrusions. Anchors on the exact tool family names used to move from a service/valid account to SYSTEM. Rationale: Anchors on the three Potato variant names the article explicitly attributes to privilege escalation (GodPotato, SweetPotato, BadPotato); these are offensive-only tool names, so name/cmdline matches are high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/incidents-at-brazilian-educational-institutions/120803/
ATT&CKT1134.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red-team / pentest engagement running Potato tools with authorization
  • Security researcher detonating the tools in a sandbox VM
  • A file legitimately containing the substring 'potato' in an unrelated business name (rare, mitigated by path/cmdline context)
  • Malware-analysis training lab
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Tools\RedTeam\", @"\PurpleTeam\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating (pre-escalation) account and whether the resulting process/child ran at SYSTEM integrity; review parent process (often a service or web-app pool identity). 2) Contain: isolate the host and reset credentials for the abused service/valid account. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for follow-on SYSTEM-level actions — Defender-disable batch scripts, RDP enablement (fDenyTSConnections=0), PsExec spread, and ransomware payload drops.
DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName has_any ("GodPotato","SweetPotato","BadPotato")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("GodPotato","SweetPotato","BadPotato")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("GodPotato","SweetPotato","BadPotato")
    or CommandLine has_any ("GodPotato","SweetPotato","BadPotato")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AnyDesk silent/unattended install used for DragonForce access AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the attacker-driven AnyDesk deployment the article ties to DragonForce (Case 02): AnyDesk installed and configured for unattended access to give operators remote control before ransomware. Anchors on the unattended-install command-line flags rather than mere presence of AnyDesk. Rationale: Anchors on AnyDesk (named in Case 02 as the DragonForce remote-access vector) combined with unattended-install flags that legitimate interactive users rarely pass, corroborated by DragonForce write-ups documenting silent AnyDesk installs for persistence. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/dragonforce-ransomware-attack/ • https://www.intel471.com/blog/dragonforce-ransomware
ATT&CKT1219 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT helpdesk legitimately deploying AnyDesk unattended via GPO/RMM
  • MSP standardizing on AnyDesk for remote support with --start-with-win
  • User self-installing AnyDesk from a legit MSI that passes --silent
  • Vendor support session where AnyDesk is provisioned with a set password
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("AnyDesk.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the installing account and parent process (deployment tool vs. email client vs. script) and whether AnyDesk is a sanctioned tool for this host/OU. 2) Contain: if unsanctioned, isolate the host, kill AnyDesk, and rotate credentials; capture the AnyDesk ID/anydesk.trace for the incoming operator IP. 3) Hunt: check DeviceNetworkEvents for AnyDesk relay traffic (boot.net.anydesk.com / *.relay), then look for DragonForce indicators — PsExec spread, mass encryption, ransom notes — across hosts that ran AnyDesk in the same window.

| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent

| where CommandLine has_any ("--install","--silent","--start-with-win","--set-password")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;

Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-08-03 10 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Explore how passkey implementation gaps undermine security when relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor. The post Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.002 T1555.003 T1566 T1574.002
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance
Detected
Phase 2
Weaponization
—
Phase 3
Delivery
Detected

Exploitation
Detected

Installation
Detected

Detected
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Chrome process accessing Google Chrome synced-passkey LevelDB store · [LLM] Command line referencing Chrome Sync Data LevelDB passkey path (copy/stage for exfil) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Non-Chrome process accessing Google Chrome synced-passkey LevelDB store AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Pass-ta-key 'Stage Zero' reconnaissance/extraction step where endpoint malware reads or writes Chrome's synced-passkey store (WebauthnCredentialSpecifics records) under '\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\Sync Data\LevelDB' to enumerate passkey usage and lift encrypted private keys. Legitimately only chrome.exe and Google updater components touch this folder, so any other process is a strong signal. Rationale: Uses the article's most concrete artifact: the exact Chrome synced-passkey store path '\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\Sync Data\LevelDB' holding WebauthnCredentialSpecifics records. Only chrome.exe/Google components legitimately touch it, so a non-Google process reading/writing there is high-fidelity. Path and behaviour corroborated by BleepingComputer and The Hacker News write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-pass-ta-key-attacks-let-malware-hijack-google-synced-passkeys/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html • https://gbhackers.com/malware-can-steal-googles-synced-passkeys/amp/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1217
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Endpoint/browser backup agents (Code42, Druva, Acronis) snapshotting the Chrome profile folder
  • DLP or EDR file-integrity scanners enumerating AppData
  • Chrome profile migration/repair utilities run by IT during troubleshooting
  • Antivirus on-access scanning of the Sync Data directory
  • User-initiated profile export via third-party Chrome data-transfer tools
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code42service.exe","crashplanservice.exe","druva-insync.exe","acronis_agent.exe","msmpeng.exe","mssense.exe","sensendr.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify InitiatingProcess (name, path, SHA256, signer) and whether it is a known backup/AV/IT tool; check if the process is signed and previously seen on the host. Pull its full command line and parent. 2) Contain: If the process is unsigned, dropped in a user-writable temp path, or unknown, isolate the host and kill/quarantine the binary; treat all passkeys registered from that account as compromised and force re-enrollment plus revocation of active sessions. 3) Hunt: Search the same host for reads of the Chrome Local State / 'Login Data' files, chrome.exe process-memory access (SDS master-key theft), and outbound transfer of copied LevelDB files; sweep the fleet for the same InitiatingProcessSHA256.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FolderPath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\" and FolderPath has @"\Sync Data\LevelDB"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","googleupdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","googlecrashhandler.exe","googlecrashhandler64.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Ops=count(), Actions=make_set(ActionType), Files=make_set(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\" and TargetFilePath has @"\Sync Data\LevelDB"
| where ActingProcessName !has "chrome.exe" and ActingProcessName !has "GoogleUpdate" and ActingProcessName !has "elevation_service" and ActingProcessName !has "software_reporter_tool"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Ops=count(), Files=make_set(TargetFileName) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Non-Chrome Process Touching Chrome Synced-Passkey LevelDB Store
id: 6f3c1e2a-9d4b-4c8e-8a1f-2b7d9e0c5a11
description: Detects a non-Chrome / non-Google process performing file operations on Chrome's synced passkey store (Sync Data\LevelDB), used by Pass-ta-key malware to enumerate and extract synced passkeys.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication-security-risks/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-pass-ta-key-attacks-let-malware-hijack-google-synced-passkeys/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/07
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1217
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains|all:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
      - '\Sync Data\LevelDB'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
      - '\elevation_service.exe'
      - '\software_reporter_tool.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:*Chrome?User?Data* (@TargetFilename:*Sync?Data?LevelDB* OR @TargetFilename:*Sync?Data?leveldb*) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\GoogleUpdate.exe OR *\elevation_service.exe OR *\software_reporter_tool.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\.*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(chrome|GoogleUpdate|elevation_service|software_reporter_tool)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\*" AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","GoogleCrashHandler.exe","GoogleCrashHandler64.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Sync Data\\LevelDB\\*" AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","elevation_service.exe","software_reporter_tool.exe","GoogleCrashHandler.exe","GoogleCrashHandler64.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Command line referencing Chrome Sync Data LevelDB passkey path (copy/stage for exfil) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts LOLBins, archivers and copy utilities whose command line references Chrome's synced-passkey store path, indicating the Golden Pass-ta-key extraction step where an attacker copies or archives the Sync Data\LevelDB folder to stage synced passkey private keys for exfiltration. Complements the file-event UC by catching read/copy operations that reference the path on the command line. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact store path 'Chrome\User Data\...\Sync Data\LevelDB' appearing in a process command line — the signature of archive/copy tooling (esentutl, robocopy, tar, 7z, powershell Copy-Item) staging synced passkeys for exfil. Distinct pivot (process command line) from the file-event UC; catches read/copy that DeviceFileEvents cannot log. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-pass-ta-key-attacks-let-malware-hijack-google-synced-passkeys/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1005 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT admin manually copying a Chrome profile with robocopy/xcopy during user migration
  • Backup scripts explicitly referencing the profile path in scheduled tasks
  • Security researcher / forensic acquisition on a managed host
  • PowerShell profile-repair one-liners referencing Sync Data during Chrome troubleshooting
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","gpscript.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "taskeng.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Review the full command line and the parent process — determine whether it is an interactive admin action, a scheduled backup, or an unexpected spawn (e.g. from a script host, Office, or a temp-dir binary). Capture the acting binary hash. 2) Contain: If unauthorized, isolate the host, kill the process and preserve any archive it created (check for .zip/.7z/.tar containing the LevelDB); force passkey re-enrollment and session revocation for the affected Google account. 3) Hunt: Look for subsequent outbound transfer of the staged archive, chrome.exe process-memory reads (SDS master-key theft), and reuse of the same parent process or acting binary across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine contains @"\Sync Data\LevelDB" or (ProcessCommandLine contains @"Chrome\User Data" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Sync Data")
| where FileName !in~ ("chrome.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine contains @"\Sync Data\LevelDB" or (CommandLine contains @"Chrome\User Data" and CommandLine contains "Sync Data")
| where NewProcessName !endswith "\\chrome.exe"
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Command Line Referencing Chrome Synced-Passkey LevelDB Path
id: b2a7d4c1-3e59-4f6a-9c2d-71e8f0a4b622
description: Detects a non-Chrome process launched with a command line referencing Chrome's Sync Data\LevelDB passkey store, consistent with copy/archive staging of synced passkeys (Golden Pass-ta-key extraction).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication-security-risks/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/google-password-manager-attacks-could.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/07
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains: '\Sync Data\LevelDB'
  filter_chrome:
    Image|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_chrome
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@CommandLine:*Sync?Data?LevelDB* OR @CommandLine:*Sync?Data?leveldb*) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/Sync Data\\LevelDB/i
| ImageFileName!=/\\chrome\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*Sync Data\\LevelDB*" AND NOT Processes.process_name="chrome.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*Sync Data\\LevelDB*" AND NOT Processes.process_name="chrome.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
